direction: Keep approved Dong Ho drawing style; communicate game action rather than isolated motifs. No elephants.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / mobile game icon concept.
These three user-supplied Đông Hồ prints are the visual source. The user APPROVES the print style and REJECTS isolated faces, houses and flags as the game's icon because they do not communicate gameplay. Keep the approved style but turn the subject into a compelling ACTION, with an unmistakable historical warfare / strategy-game feeling.

Style references: Image 1's flat, expressive mounted figures and poses; Image 2's simple white horse, green harness and broadly blocked historical garments; Image 3's bold swollen shapes, green/red rhythm, decisive irregular black outlines and economical expressive marks. Adapt this drawing language faithfully. Broad forest-green, vermilion, ochre, indigo and shell-cream pigment blocks, confident black contour, subtle print grain INSIDE the shapes. No 3D or photorealistic lighting, no metal shine, no dense hatching, no fantasy filigree. This should be a beautiful and exciting GAME ICON painted as a Đông Hồ print, with a dynamic silhouette and a clear moment of action. Historical game illustration, not a reconstruction of a named person's likeness or an authenticated dynasty costume.

Square mobile composition, a strong close composition built from TWO OR THREE BIG READABLE MASSES; not a crowded full battle painting. Limit background to one simple flat ground/water shape. All vital subject features inside the central 78% for launcher corners, no large empty decorative margins. Bold enough to read at 64px. Opaque shell-cream background to all four edges. No inset frame, museum paper border, writing, numbers, UI, card border, logos, seals or lettering. NO ELEPHANT in any form. No standalone face, house, flag, bird logo or decorative heraldic emblem. One finished square PNG, ideally 1024x1024.

CONCEPT A — LEAD THE CHARGE. Compress the idea of commanding cavalry into one powerful, unified silhouette: a heroic Vietnamese folk-print RIDER on a WHITE HORSE charging diagonally forward toward the viewer's right. Horse neck raised, one front leg reaching forward and one bent, hindquarters pushing off, compact curled ochre/black mane and one bold green harness. The rider leans forward with purpose, wears a simple vermilion coat, green sash and compact cloth cap derived from the reference, and holds one long spear angled forward above the horse's head. Their body, spear and horse create one flowing thrust through the square. Keep the rider's small face to three expressive ink marks; no portrait detail. Use minimal ochre dust curls beneath the hooves as a single subordinate shape. NO FLAG, opposing army, landscape, floating objects or ornate armor. Make the horse and rider feel like an exciting controllable unit charging in a strategy game, not a procession or ceremonial parade.

CONCEPT B — BREAK THEIR FORMATION. Show ONE highly legible tactical encounter from Vạn Thắng's actual core combat: a compact wedge of THREE vermilion-clad spearmen pushing from the lower left toward a compact wall of THREE dark-green shield soldiers at the upper right. View from a slightly raised folk-print oblique angle, shallow perspective. The two formations are the two principal graphic masses, almost filling the icon. Each figure is deliberately chunky and very simple: a small head, broad tunic, two stout legs, one clear weapon or round shield. Simple historical cloth caps/headwraps; no modern uniform, no Western helmets, no elaborate armor. The spear shafts converge toward ONE central clash point against the nearest broad ochre shield, with one small cream jagged contact burst. A clear diagonal gap between the red wedge and green wall makes opposition and tactics readable. The humans have tiny expressive faces only, no portrait closeups. No blood, bodies or gore. No army banners, buildings, trees, scenery, interface or battle diagram arrows. Dynamic, warm, beautifully designed folk-art game combat with unmistakable two-team tension; simplify hard enough that this does not become six tiny detailed portraits.

CONCEPT C — THE RIVER TRAP. Make a compact action icon inspired by the game's Bạch Đằng river-stakes story: ONE broad dark-green wooden enemy warboat with a single ochre battened sail tilts as its bow meets THREE large pointed brown river stakes rising from bold curling indigo waves. The boat, the triangular stake cluster, and one broad S-curve of water are the only three graphic masses. The diagonal boat silhouette points down toward the stakes; a simple ivory splash at the bow makes the collision and tactical ambush immediately clear. No people needed. The boat is a symbolic historic game vessel, not a detailed maritime reconstruction. Draw the sail as one full bold ochre shape divided by only two black battens; no rigging web, lanterns, dragons, pagoda cabins, flags, labels or tiny details. Use the rhythmic curves and expressive outline of the supplied pig print to shape the wave and the hull. The action should feel clever, dramatic and rewarding: the trap has worked. Only a little shell-cream negative space surrounds the action, no landscape panorama. A Vietnamese history strategy-game promise, not a peaceful sailing or travel icon.
